history.label: A number's history
history.help: What the order page shows beside an order, and what the risk score reads: the number's other orders and what became of them. "Earlier orders read": how many of its past orders count, newest first. "Refusals that are our fault": refusal reasons (from "Parcel refusal reasons") that never count against the customer — arrived late, the wrong item, damaged, after Eid, did not order; such a parcel is shown as "our fault, not counted" and never raises the score. "Unanswered call outcomes": the call screen's results that mean the customer did not pick up.

score.label: Risk score
score.help: When on, every new order gets a risk score the moment it lands: the signals below that apply, each with its weight, added up (at most 100). The score, its band and the reasons are kept on the order and in its timeline, and they never change by themselves; an edit by the team scores the order again ("after an edit"), as a new line. The score only informs the team: nothing is blocked, held, asked in advance or changed by it. "Show on the order": the order page shows the risk card. Off: no order is scored.

signals.label: Risk signals and weights
signals.help: Each signal has its own switch and weight (0–100), and the numbers it looks at. From the number's history: refused parcels (not our fault), cancelled orders (only the reasons you tick), the share of parcels taken at the door, a first order, unanswered calls, another order in the last hours, a parcel already on its way, a high order value (your amount; empty: never). From the address: no place found, the place not sure, no house details, a different district than the number is known by, your list of places, many refusals at the same place. PR 541 adds, both off: many pieces in one order (your number; empty: never), and the same person under another number — earlier orders of another number with the same name and an address this alike, a refusal among them named. Same device, another number (off): earlier orders from this device under another number. Many numbers from one connection (off): other numbers ordered from the same connection within the hours you set.

names.successRatio: Few parcels taken at the door
names.recentOrder: Another order in the last hours
names.inTransit: A parcel is already on its way

bands.label: Risk bands
bands.help: The levels a score falls into, each from its lowest score up to the next band's. The first starts at 0 and the thresholds rise. Each band has its name in English and Bengali and its colour (green, amber, red). What happens at a level — watch, hold, a call, an advance — is set with the risk rules' actions.

sections.label: Order sections
sections.help: When on, every new order is placed in one section the moment it lands, with a note on its timeline, so the order list shows each order already sorted: possible duplicate, re-order (another order open or on its way — the signals you pick), new identity (the same person under another number — the signals you pick), high risk and watch (the bands you pick), prepaid (never in the call queue; a flagged prepaid order is still reviewed) and clear. "Wait for a person": orders in these sections are neither confirmed nor booked until someone decides (approve, hold, ask the customer or decline). Marking is instant; the decision never is: nothing is cancelled, blocked, held or changed by itself.

capture.label: What the checkout keeps for the checks
capture.help: The connection (IP) and the shop's own device code are kept with each order; the customer's location only when he taps "Share my location", rounded. All three are deleted from the order after the days you set (180 unless you change it). They only inform the risk checks; nobody is blocked by them.

identity.label: One identity per customer
identity.help: When on, every new order is linked to one identity the moment it lands (and again when the team edits the phone, the name or the address): orders with the same phone, the same device, or a name and an address that are alike (spelling a little off still matches) belong to the same person, so a customer who changes his number is still known. The connection (IP) never joins two orders by itself, because many people share one mobile connection; it is only counted. While this is on, the risk signals "same person under another number" and "same device" read this identity. How far back a match reaches (days, 0 = ever), how alike the name and the address must be (1 = the same text), whether the same device joins two numbers, and how many earlier orders one step reads. It only records and informs: nothing is blocked, held or cancelled by it.

duplicateRules.label: Duplicate & re-order rules
duplicateRules.help: When on, every new order is checked against these rules instead of the one look-back of the duplicate check (whose own switch still turns the whole check off). Each rule has its own switch, its window in minutes (how far back the other order may be; 0 = no limit), the confidence a match needs (0–100) and what it proposes: cancel (the review proposes cancelling it as a duplicate), hold (the review waits for a person), warn (a note on the timeline only) or allow (recorded, nothing else). There is no block action, and a rule never acts by itself: with cancel or hold the order is neither confirmed nor booked until a person decides. "The same customer" is the same account, the same phone, or — while "One identity per customer" is on — the same identity. A: the same items again while the first is not yet with the courier. B: different items in the window. C: a parcel of his is with the courier. D: an alike address under a new phone. E: the same style in another size in his other open order. H: a number, identity or address a person blocked. I: a bulk-looking order (at least the pieces you set, in this order or with his open orders in the window).

scenario.C: A parcel of his is with the courier

levels.label: What happens at each risk level
levels.help: Off until you switch it on. For each risk band (low, medium, high) you choose what follows when an order lands in it: a watch mark, a hold with your hold reason (the order is not confirmed or sent until a person releases it), a confirmation call task, and what the customer is asked to pay first — nothing, the delivery charge, a part, the whole amount, or no cash on delivery for this order. Watch, hold and call run by themselves only while switched on. The payment ask is always a proposal on the order page: a person presses "Request advance". Nothing here blocks anyone or changes a COD rule, a price or a charge. The partial percent is yours to set; until then the partial ask cannot be used.

blocklist.label: Blocklist
blocklist.help: Phone numbers a person listed, each with the reason, who and when; Undo keeps the line with who undid it and why. When on, a new order from a listed number (or the same person under another number) is marked for the team, or held for a person to decide. Nothing is ever cancelled and the customer is never told. Off as shipped.

refusers.label: Repeat refusers
refusers.help: Numbers that refused parcels again and again (not our fault), from how many refusals you set. You choose per case what the number's new orders get: nothing, the delivery charge first, the full amount first, or no cash on delivery — with a reason, and you can end it any time. When on, the terms reach a new order as a proposal that a person sends. Nothing changes COD by itself. Off as shipped.

report.label: Fraud report
report.help: How many days Reports › Fraud & RTO shows when no dates are picked (30 as shipped), and the most orders and returned parcels one report reads (5,000 as shipped; past it the page says the figures are cut short). The report only reads: it never blocks anyone, cancels an order or moves money.

bundling.label: One parcel for one person's orders
bundling.help: When on, a new order looks for the same person's other open orders (the same identity or number) to the same address, placed within the hours you set, not yet with the courier. "Propose" (as shipped) marks the order so a person presses "One parcel"; "Group" puts them in one parcel by itself. Each order keeps its lines, prices, charges and payments; nothing is cancelled or blocked. Until you set the hours, nothing happens. Off as shipped.

blockProposal.label: Propose numbers for the blocklist
blockProposal.help: When on, a new order from a person (the number, or the same person under another number) with at least the rejections you set — parcels refused at the door (not your fault, never a try-on) plus orders cancelled with the codes you tick — proposes the number for the blocklist, with the names and addresses given and every product ordered with its date. A person blocks it or says "Not now"; nothing is blocked by itself and the order goes on as usual. Until you set the number, nothing is proposed. Off as shipped.

goodCustomer.label: Good customers are never held by the engine
goodCustomer.help: When on, a customer with at least the delivered orders you set and at most the refusals you allow (counted as the phone history counts them) is never held by the engine by itself: the duplicate check's automatic hold, a risk level's hold and its automatic advance request are skipped, and the order says "good customer". A review still opens for a person. Until you set the number, nobody counts as one. Off as shipped.

stopReport.label: Stopped by the engine — the weekly report
stopReport.help: How many days the report shows (a week as shipped), when a rule is flagged (the share of its stopped orders that were delivered all the same; empty: never), the fewest stops before it can be flagged, and the most orders one report lists. The report only reads.

approval.label: The engine acts only with your OK
approval.help: When on, the risk engine acts on nothing by itself: the duplicate check's, a risk level's and the blocklist's holds become proposed holds that a person holds or lets go, "one parcel by itself" stays a proposal, and no advance is asked by itself, whatever those switches say. Today's digest lists what waits. Also the most rows each waiting list shows. Off as shipped.

learning.label: Learn from the team's decisions
learning.help: Every decision a person takes on what the engine stopped or proposed is kept with its note. When on, Reports › Decisions & learning shows, per rule and per person, how often people let the engine's stop go or kept it and how the orders let go ended; a rule decided often enough that people mostly let go (or mostly keep) gets a suggestion, and an open review shows what people did with ones like it. It only suggests: no rule changes by itself. Also how many days it reads, the fewest decisions before it says anything, the share for a suggestion and the most decisions one report reads. Off as shipped.

newCustomer.label: Call a new customer once
newCustomer.help: When on, a customer with no earlier order anywhere in the shop — not by this number in any form, the account, or the same person under another number — gets one call on the first order (Orders › Calls to make), a "New customer" mark and a timeline line. Never a hold, a decline or an advance, and it adds nothing to the risk score. Prepaid orders get the call only when "prepaid" is on. Off as shipped.

callOutcomes.label: Call outcomes
callOutcomes.help: What a person records after a call on Orders › Calls to make, each with its English and Bengali words and whether it closes the call; the others keep the call in the list for the next try. Recording a call never changes the order.

transitDuplicate.label: Parcel already on its way
transitDuplicate.help: When on, the moment a whole phone number is typed at checkout the shop looks for this customer's order that is already on its way (or any open order, if chosen) with the very piece in the bag — same product, colour and size. The checkout shows the piece, the earlier order's number and its tracking link, and two buttons: take it out, or "No, I want another one". The order's number and link show only when that order was placed from this browser or account; a match by the number alone shows nothing unless "by the number alone" is on (then without them). Every notice is kept with the campaign that brought the customer, for the report. Nothing is cancelled or blocked. With "size exchange" on, the same product and colour in another size already on its way offers an exchange on arrival instead of a second parcel. Off as shipped.
